items.title: Finitistic trees, level products, density, and matrices
items.statement: In ZF, a finitistic tree is rooted, has only finite node heights and finite levels, and has no terminal node. A set is (h,k)-dense when above some height-h root it dominates the frontier k levels later. For finitely many trees, the level product uses one common level, the full product permits different levels, and a product of coordinatewise (h,k)-dense sets is an (h,k)-matrix.
items.strategy: Fix extension as the tree order and prove the elementary domination and cone-restriction laws, including extension of finitely many unequal cone roots to the common maximum height. Keep level and full products distinct and treat k=0 explicitly.
items.axiom_base: ZF; all selections are from explicitly coded finite sets

items.title: The finite word calculus for the Halpern–Läuchli argument
items.statement: For positive finite d, L_d consists of length-2d words containing for each coordinate either existential-matrix before universal-node or universal-matrix before existential-node. Its derivability relation is generated by the three source rule classes: like-quantifier commutations, matched-pair replacement, and finite block permutation.
items.strategy: List every atom and rule scheme with its side condition that the result remains in L_d, and define derivability by a finite rule sequence. No semantic assertion is included in the syntax definition.

items.title: Finite word-calculus rearrangement
items.statement: For every positive finite d, the all-universal-matrix/all-existential-node endpoint word derives the all-existential-matrix/all-universal-node endpoint word.
items.strategy: Induct on d, exposing the last obstructing pair by commutations, switching it by the matched-pair rule, and restoring normal form by the block rule. Print the d=1 derivation and verify membership in L_d at every step.

items.title: Soundness of the three word rules and density-preserving finite thinning
items.statement: Under the matrix/node interpretation of words for Q in a finite tree product, truth is monotone under shrinking universally quantified coordinate sets. If W derives W', then the scheme forall n exists p Phi(W,n,p) implies forall n exists p Phi(W',n,p); Rule 3 changes the density parameters by a finite thinning that preserves the required domination.
items.strategy: Define Phi exactly and prove preservation of its quantified scheme, not pointwise preservation at fixed density parameters. Handle Rules 1 and 2 by the valid quantifier interchange and the finite displayed-witness construction. For Rule 3, enumerate the finite root tuples and thin coordinate frontiers successively, preserving domination at a later level. Every recursion is finite and least natural density witnesses can be used, so no countable choice is hidden.

items.title: Halpern–Läuchli dense-matrix dichotomy
items.statement: In ZF, for a positive finite family of finitistic trees without terminal nodes and Q in their full product, either Q contains a k-matrix for every k, or for some h its complement contains an (h,k)-matrix for every k.
items.strategy: Interpret the endpoint words and apply rearrangement plus soundness. In the complement case extend the finitely many cone roots to h=max n_i, then restrict the p=h+k dense frontiers to those cones; the cone lemma gives the required (h,k)-matrix. This supplies the design-mandated common-height repair.
items.axiom_base: ZF; positive finite dimension is essential

items.title: Finite level-product partition theorem by the compactness tree
items.statement: For fixed positive finite d and q, some finite truncation height n forces every q-coloring of the truncated product to contain a monochromatic (h,1)-matrix for some h<n; the terminal common-level form follows by domination.
items.strategy: If every n admits a bad coloring, form the finite-level tree of bad colorings ordered by restriction and apply Konig's lemma to obtain a coherent branch. The resulting infinite coloring contradicts the dichotomy, using induction on q for the positive alternative. Derive the terminal-level form by the domination principle. State AC exactly at the Konig-lemma invocation; no choice is used in the dense-matrix input.
items.axiom_base: ZFC for the compactness-tree branch; the dense-matrix input is ZF

items.title: Finite partial prime-ideal diagrams
items.statement: For a finite Boolean subalgebra A of a Boolean algebra B, a finite partial prime-ideal diagram is a Boolean homomorphism e:A→2; e^{-1}(0) is its partial ideal side. For finite F⊆B, the diagram deciding F is taken on the finite subalgebra generated by F.
items.strategy: Construct the generated subalgebra from the finitely many Boolean cells of F, delete the zero cells, and use truth values so complement and primeness are symmetric. Requiring a homomorphism on the whole finite subalgebra records all algebraic consequences and avoids a spurious locally-consistent partial assignment.

items.title: Extension of finite partial prime-ideal diagrams
items.statement: If A⊆C are finite Boolean subalgebras of B, every homomorphism e:A→2 extends to a homomorphism e':C→2. Consequently every finite partial prime-ideal diagram extends across any prescribed finite subset of B.
items.strategy: The homomorphism e selects a unique atom a of A. The finitely many atoms of C below a have join a, so at least one is nonzero; one such atom gives a principal ultrafilter and hence a homomorphism C→2 extending e. For prescribed F, take C generated by A∪F. This is a single finite existence argument and uses no choice principle or unstated ordering.
items.axiom_base: ZF; a single finite existential witness, not a choice function

items.title: The compactness tree yields a prime ideal for an enumerated Boolean algebra
items.statement: In ZF, every nontrivial Boolean algebra supplied with a surjection from omega has a prime ideal; equivalently, every countable finitely satisfiable Boolean diagram has a two-valued solution.
items.strategy: Let B_n be the finite subalgebra generated by the first n enumerated elements and put all homomorphisms B_n→2 at level n, ordered by restriction. The finite-extension lemma makes every level nonempty. Recursively choose the lexicographically least node having extensions at arbitrarily high levels; finite branching shows the chosen node has such a child. The union is a total homomorphism B→2, and its zero fibre is a proper prime ideal. Check enumeration repetitions and nontriviality.
items.axiom_base: ZF; the supplied enumeration and binary least choices avoid countable choice

items.title: BPI and the set ultrafilter lemma are equivalent over ZF
items.statement: Over ZF, the Boolean Prime Ideal principle is equivalent to the set ultrafilter lemma that every proper filter on a set extends to an ultrafilter.
items.strategy: For BPI→UFL, quotient P(S) by the ideal dual to the supplied filter, take a prime ideal, and pull back its complementary filter. For UFL→BPI, let X be the set of finite partial homomorphisms B→2 and let D_b contain those deciding b. Finite Boolean subalgebras show the family {D_b:b∈B} has the finite-intersection property. Extend its generated set filter to an ultrafilter U and set h(b)=i when {p∈D_b:p(b)=i} lies in U. Finite intersections make h a total Boolean homomorphism; h^{-1}(0) is prime. Treat empty carriers and the trivial algebra separately.
items.axiom_base: ZF; no form of Choice in either implication

items.title: The Halpern–Läuchli theorem and the basic Cohen BPI model
items.statement: The finite-product Halpern–Läuchli theorem holds in ZF, and the basic Cohen symmetric model supplied by the preceding page is a transitive ZF model of BPI plus not AC. These are separate modules; the combinatorial proof does not supply symmetric-name support analysis.
items.strategy: Compose the choice-free dense-matrix theorem with the independent HS search-and-shift theorem for the basic Cohen BPI model, keeping the two modules and their axiom bases explicit.
items.axiom_base: ZF internally; exact metatheory is inherited only from the verified Batch 7 suppliers

references.title: Brian Ransom, On BPI in Symmetric Extensions Part 1
references.locator: Theorem 3.10, Lemma 4.6, Theorem 4.9, and Theorem 5.27–Corollary 5.28 and their complete proofs in Sections 3–5

references.title: J. D. Halpern and A. Lévy, The Boolean prime ideal theorem does not imply the axiom of choice

items.title: Relative consistency of BPI without Choice together with Halpern–Läuchli
items.statement: Con(ZF) implies Con(ZF+BPI+not AC plus the finite-product Halpern–Läuchli dense-matrix scheme); hence, conditional on Con(ZF), BPI does not imply AC.
items.strategy: Add the finitely many Halpern–Läuchli instances in any alleged target refutation by substituting their fixed ZF proofs. This converts that refutation externally into one of ZF+BPI+not-AC and contradicts the basic-Cohen relative-consistency result; no arithmetized uniform transformer is claimed.

references.title: Brian Ransom, On BPI in Symmetric Extensions Part 1
references.locator: Theorem 3.10, Lemma 4.6, Theorem 4.9, and Theorem 5.27–Corollary 5.28 and their complete proofs in Sections 3–5

references.title: J. D. Halpern and A. Lévy, The Boolean prime ideal theorem does not imply the axiom of choice

items.title: Strict relative placement of BPI between ZF and Choice
items.statement: Under the exact consistency antecedents of the two model constructions, BPI is neither provable in ZF nor sufficient for AC. These are conditional formal consistency/nonprovability statements, not assertions that any theory is consistent.
items.strategy: Use the basic-Cohen result for failure of BPI-to-AC. For nonprovability in ZF, BPI and the set ultrafilter lemma would extend the cofinite filter on omega to a free ultrafilter, contradicting the certified relative-consistency model with no such ultrafilter. Preserve both consistency antecedents.

references.locator: Theorem 3.10, Lemma 4.6, Theorem 4.9, and Theorem 5.27–Corollary 5.28 and their complete proofs in Sections 3–5

references.title: J. D. Halpern and A. Lévy, The Boolean prime ideal theorem does not imply the axiom of choice

title: Halpern–Läuchli and BPI without Choice: Examples and Counterexamples

items.title: A two-tree level product and dense matrix
items.statement: In two full binary trees, compute a common level product, a full-product pair of mixed heights, and an (h,k)-matrix, demonstrating that the three notions differ.
items.strategy: List the level-2 pairs, select one cone in each coordinate, list its height h+k frontier, and exhibit a mixed-height full-product pair.

items.title: The common-height cone repair in the complement case
items.statement: Binary-tree cone roots at different heights are extended to their common maximum height before dense frontiers are restricted.
items.strategy: Use roots of heights one and three, set h=3, extend the first root, and verify directly that restricting an (h+k)-dense frontier to both cones is coordinatewise (h,k)-dense.

items.title: A dimension-two Halpern–Läuchli word rearrangement
items.statement: For d=2, display a complete legal derivation between the endpoint words.
items.strategy: Print every intermediate word, label its rule and coordinate permutation, and verify the within-coordinate precedence condition.

items.title: A prime-ideal compactness tree for the finite–cofinite algebra
items.statement: For the finite–cofinite Boolean algebra on omega, compute initial partial-diagram levels and the branch whose zero fibre is the finite-set ideal.
items.strategy: Using the finite-diagram definition, enumerate finite sets and complements in paired order, list early homomorphism levels, and directly verify that evaluation at each cofinite remainder gives a coherent branch whose union has the finite-set ideal as proper prime zero fibre.

items.title: BPI well-orders every set
items.statement: BPI does not imply that every set is well-orderable. Whenever the basic Cohen construction hypotheses are supplied, its model contains a concrete non-well-orderable Dedekind-finite set; conditional on Con(ZF), the corresponding syntactic nonimplication follows from the relative-consistency theorem.
items.strategy: In the certified basic Cohen model, BPI holds while the infinite Dedekind-finite Cohen set is not well-orderable: a well-order would recursively select the least unused member and produce an injection from omega. For the conditional syntactic conclusion, derive AC directly from universal well-orderability by choosing the least member of each nonempty set, then invoke relative consistency of BPI with not-AC.

references.title: Brian Ransom, On BPI in Symmetric Extensions Part 1
references.locator: Theorem 3.10, Lemma 4.6, Theorem 4.9, and Theorem 5.27–Corollary 5.28 and their complete proofs in Sections 3–5

references.title: J. D. Halpern and A. Lévy, The Boolean prime ideal theorem does not imply the axiom of choice

title: Solovay's Model and Regularity of All Sets of Reals

items.title: The inaccessible Lévy-collapse setup for Solovay's construction
items.statement: From a transitive U satisfying ZFC with inaccessible kappa, take the constructible forcing ground V=L^U, where kappa remains inaccessible and every ground parameter has an ordinal code. Force with finite-condition Coll(omega,<kappa), and let G be a supplied V-generic. For xi<kappa, G_xi is the induced initial-collapse generic. Existence of U or G is not asserted.
items.strategy: Use the constructible inner-model theorem, downward regularity, preservation of ground cardinals, and GCH in L to preserve the inaccessible while obtaining a canonical ordinal code for every ground parameter. Then match Solovay's partial-function order to the published Lévy forcing and define the initial complete suborders and quotient generics. Ground AC supplies cardinal comparisons, maximal antichains, and forcing recursion; it is not asserted in the inner model.
items.axiom_base: Ambient ZFC plus an inaccessible and a supplied generic

items.title: The Lévy collapse localizes countable ordinal data
items.statement: In V[G], kappa=omega_1; every real and countable ordinal sequence belongs to some V[G_xi], xi<kappa; and each such intermediate model's reals are countable in V[G].
items.strategy: Use the forcing decision-density lemma and ambient AC to choose maximal antichains deciding the countably many name coordinates, then use kappa-cc and regularity to bound the union of their supports below kappa. The tail collapse makes the intermediate real set countable.

items.title: Absorption, factorization, and homogeneous truth in the Solovay collapse
items.statement: For every countable ordinal sequence f in V[G], some real t and ordinal beta define f in V[t], and V[G]=V[f][H] for a Lévy-collapse generic H over V[f]. Sentences with parameters from V[f] that omit H are decided by homogeneity. Analogous factorizations hold after adjoining a random or Cohen real.
items.strategy: Localize f to a small collapse, use the constructible ground order plus the collapsed deciding data to capture f by a real and an ordinal-coded name, and apply the absorption isomorphism. Move any two tail conditions to compatible conditions by a coordinate permutation to prove zero-one Boolean values. Track parameters and the omitted generic explicitly.
items.axiom_base: Ambient ZFC; AC enters through forcing and Boolean completions

items.title: The hereditarily ordinal-sequence-definable Solovay model
items.statement: Inside V[G], let S be the class of countable ordinal sequences and M=HOD(S), the sets hereditarily definable from one member of S and finitely many ordinals. M is not definitionally identified with L(R) or HOD(R).
items.strategy: Give the uniform set-level definition through transitive closure and satisfaction codes. Explain how localized collapse data lets a real code the relevant countable ordinal parameter, but assert no equality among the three standard inner models.

items.title: L(R) in the Solovay collapse extension
items.statement: In the Levy-collapse extension V[G], let L(R) be the least transitive inner model containing every ordinal and every real of V[G]. It has the same reals and ordinals as V[G] and is contained in the hereditarily ordinal-sequence-definable Solovay model, but the two models are not identified.
items.strategy: Build the relativized constructible hierarchy over the predicate R^{V[G]}. Verify transitivity and minimality. Every real is a countable ordinal sequence, so the defining parameters place L(R) inside HOD(S), while the reverse inclusion is neither asserted nor needed.

references.title: Unger, A Brief Account of Solovay's Model
references.locator: opening discussion of HOD(S), L(R), and HOD(R), pp.1-2

items.title: The Solovay inner model satisfies ZF and every real set has a real–ordinal definition
items.statement: M is a transitive ZF inner model with the same ordinals and reals as V[G]. Every A⊆R in M is definable in V[G] from a real and finitely many ordinals, equivalently from a countable ordinal sequence.
items.strategy: Adapt the HOD proof formula by formula to S. For Replacement, define the image from the fixed hereditary codes of the function and domain rather than choosing codes value by value; define the internal power set by the uniform HOD(S) predicate. Combine the fixed S/ordinal parameters into one sequence, localize it, and use the constructible-ground real-capture lemma to replace the S-parameter by a real plus the ordinal code of a ground name. Since the ground is L, relativize the fixed definition over V[r]=L[r] to obtain an ambient V[G]-definition. Retain arbitrary ordinal parameters explicitly; do not infer M=L(R) or real-code uncountable ordinals.
items.axiom_base: Ambient ZFC construction; internal conclusion ZF

items.title: The Solovay inner model is closed under ambient omega-sequences
items.statement: If f∈V[G] is a function from omega into M, then f∈M.
items.strategy: Use the canonical OD(S) surjection onto HOD(S). Ambient AC chooses a formula/ordinal/S code for each f(n); interleave all countable ordinal parameters into one member of S and define f from it. This is the exact use of AC.
items.axiom_base: Ambient ZFC; AC chooses definition witnesses

items.title: The Solovay inner model satisfies Dependent Choice
items.statement: M satisfies the serial-relation Dependent Choice principle although it need not satisfy full Choice.
items.strategy: For internal nonempty A and serial R, ambient AC recursively chooses an R-chain f:omega→A. Omega-sequence closure puts f in M, where transitivity verifies it. AC is used externally in this construction, not assumed internally.

items.title: Borel-code, measure, category, and perfect-set absoluteness
items.statement: Shared well-founded Borel codes evaluate identically on shared reals in the Solovay intermediate models and uniformly yield coded open representatives modulo coded meagre sets. Coded nullness, meagreness, openness, and closedness are absolute in the directions later used; nonempty perfectness transfers only between same-real models or from an explicit pruned splitting-tree certificate. DC supplies completion and countable ideal closure.
items.strategy: Induct on Borel codes, simultaneously constructing open-mod-meagre representatives: complements use the interior of the closed complement and add the nowhere-dense boundary, while countable unions union the representatives and exceptions. Express nullness by rational open covers and meagreness by coded closed nowhere-dense covers. For perfectness require same reals or an explicit pruned splitting tree, since a closed code may gain a branch after new reals are added.
items.axiom_base: ZF for code evaluation; DC for completed measure and countable closures

items.title: Random and Cohen generics over an intermediate model are conull and comeagre
items.statement: If an intermediate transitive N has countably many reals in V[G], the N-random reals are conull and the N-Cohen-generic reals are comeagre in V[G].
items.strategy: Enumerate N-coded Borel null sets and closed nowhere-dense sets in V[G]. Their union contains every nongeneric real and remains null or meagre. Ambient AC supplies the enumeration; the corresponding closure is countable.

items.title: Homogeneous truth about a generic real has Borel representatives
items.statement: For a formula over intermediate N, an N-coded Borel set represents its truth in the final collapse extension for every N-random real; the Cohen analogue gives a Borel, hence open-mod-meagre, representative on N-Cohen generics.
items.strategy: After adjoining the random/Cohen real x, factor the final extension through the homogeneous tail R_x. Take the random/Cohen Boolean value not of phi itself but of the assertion that the top of R_x forces phi. The real-forcing truth lemma, tail homogeneity, and the tail truth lemma identify its Borel representative with final-extension truth on generic reals. Retain the restriction to generics until the exceptional null/meagre set is removed.
items.axiom_base: Ambient ZFC; AC for Boolean completions/maximal antichains

items.title: Every set of reals in the Solovay model is Lebesgue measurable
items.statement: In M, every subset of the real line is Lebesgue measurable.
items.strategy: Localize the definition of A to N and obtain an N-coded Borel B agreeing with A on N-random reals. Ambiently enumerate all N-coded null Borel sets and code their union C by one real; this code lies in M because M and the final extension have the same reals. C contains every nonrandom real. Coded absoluteness and internal completeness then show A differs from B by a subset of a null set in M.
items.axiom_base: Internal ZF+DC; ambient ZFC plus inaccessible

items.title: Every set of reals in the Solovay model has the Baire property
items.statement: In M, every subset of the real line has the property of Baire.
items.strategy: Repeat the measure argument with Cohen forcing. The N-coded Borel representative agrees with A on N-generics. Ambiently enumerate the N-coded nowhere-dense obstructions and code their union by one real; that code belongs to M because M and the final extension have the same reals. Replace the Borel representative by an open set modulo a coded meagre set and combine the two explicit M-coded witnesses.
items.axiom_base: Internal ZF+DC; ambient ZFC plus inaccessible

items.title: A perfect tree of mutually generic name interpretations
items.statement: If N is ambient-countable, Q is a small collapse in N, and a Q-name tau in N is forced new over N, then V[G] contains a perfect binary tree of branch generics, mutually generic in pairs, whose tau-interpretations are pairwise distinct and vary continuously.
items.strategy: Enumerate dense sets of the forcing and its square. At each finite stage split, meet the next one- and two-coordinate dense sets, and decide longer incompatible prefixes of tau. Fusion gives generics; decided prefixes give continuity and injectivity. Countability and ambient AC are explicit.

items.title: Every uncountable Solovay-model set of reals has a perfect subset
items.statement: In M, every uncountable subset of the real line contains a nonempty perfect subset.
items.strategy: Localize A's definition to an initial stage N and choose x in A but not N. Localize x to a later initial stage, factor the interval collapse over N, and obtain its N-name from the definition of the generic extension. Homogeneity fixes a condition forcing the name new and in A. The perfect-tree lemma embeds Cantor space continuously into A; compactness and code absoluteness put the perfect image in M. Omega-sequence closure handles the countable alternative.
items.axiom_base: Internal ZF+DC; ambient ZFC plus inaccessible

items.title: Universal real measurability transfers to finite-dimensional Euclidean spaces
items.statement: In M every subset of R^n is Lebesgue measurable for each positive finite n.
items.strategy: Reduce R^n to countably many cubes. Off dyadic null boundaries, interleave binary digits for a measure-preserving Borel bijection with an interval. Pull back arbitrary subsets, apply real measurability, restore arbitrary null-boundary subsets by completeness and DC, and take the countable union. Do not use a merely Borel non-measure-preserving isomorphism.

items.title: The Solovay model has no Vitali or Bernstein set
items.statement: M contains no Vitali selector modulo Q and no Bernstein subset of R.
items.strategy: A supplied Vitali selector contradicts universal measurability by the translate argument. For a Bernstein set B, internal DC supplies countable choice, so B and its complement cannot both be countable; the uncountable one has no perfect subset and contradicts PSP. Do not use the published AC existence clauses in reverse.

items.title: The Solovay model has no Hamel basis and no discontinuous additive real function
items.statement: In M, R has no Hamel basis over Q and every additive f:R→R is continuous and R-linear; in particular no discontinuous Cauchy solution arises from Hamel coordinates.
items.strategy: From a hypothetical basis choose one b and form the unique coefficient homomorphism. Its kernel W is proper; if W has positive measure, measurable-subgroup rigidity makes W=R, while if W is null then the countable rational cosets qb+W cover R, contradicting the positive measure of [0,1]. No new choice is used. For arbitrary additive f, the measurable sets E_n={x in [-1,1]: |f(x)|<=n} cover [-1,1], so some E_n has positive measure; Steinhaus makes f bounded near zero, and the published bounded-additive regularity theorem gives continuity and R-linearity. Do not import the AC basis-existence lemma.

items.title: The Solovay model has no Banach–Tarski decomposition
items.statement: In M, no closed ball K has a finite partition K=disjoint-union_i A_i and one rigid image g_i[A_i] per piece whose disjoint union is two disjoint congruent copies of K.
items.strategy: Fix the one-use equidecomposition formulation explicitly. Every alleged piece is measurable; internal DC supplies Countable Choice, rigid motions preserve volume, and finite additivity makes the original partition have volume V while the one-use reassembly has volume 2V. For radius zero, one image of the unique nonempty piece has one point, not two.
items.axiom_base: Internal ZF+DC and universal R^3 measurability

items.title: The Solovay model fails the full Axiom of Choice
items.statement: M does not satisfy full AC, though it satisfies DC.
items.strategy: Assume AC internally. Relativize the published ZFC Bernstein construction to M, obtaining a Bernstein set and contradicting the local exclusion. AC is used only in this reductio, not in the positive internal theory.
items.axiom_base: Internal ZF+DC; AC only as reductio hypothesis

items.title: Solovay L(R) satisfies ZF and Dependent Choice
items.statement: If kappa is inaccessible in V and G is Levy-generic collapsing every ordinal below kappa to countable, then L(R)^{V[G]} is an inner model of ZF+DC with the same reals and ordinals as V[G]; its hierarchy supplies a canonical definable surjection from Ord times R onto L(R).
items.strategy: ZF follows from the relativized constructible hierarchy. Construct the canonical Ord times R surjection onto L(R). For DC, choose the least ordinal code admitting the initial point and each successor and only then use ambient AC for real witnesses. Code the witness reals into one real; leastness recovers every ordinal, including the initial one, so the chain belongs to L(R). This is the Claim 6 argument in Unger, applied to the canonical L(R) hierarchy.

references.title: Solovay, A model of set-theory in which every set of reals is Lebesgue measurable
Unger, A Brief Account of Solovay's Model
references.locator: Claim 6 and its complete least-ordinal/real-code proof, p.2

items.axiom_audit: Ambient AC chooses real witnesses after the ordinal indices have been chosen canonically; internally the conclusion is ZF+DC.

items.title: All sets of reals in Solovay L(R) have LM, BP, and PSP
items.statement: In the same collapse extension, every set of reals in L(R) is Lebesgue measurable, has the Baire property, and has the perfect-set property. Hence the no-Vitali, no-Bernstein, no-Hamel-basis, continuous-additive-map, failure-of-choice, and no-Banach-Tarski conclusions proved for HOD(S) also hold in L(R).
items.strategy: Code a member of L(R) by the preceding canonical Ord times R surjection, localize its one real parameter, and rerun the random/Cohen arguments for the resulting canonical membership formula. For PSP, use the explicitly countable intermediate-stage reals and the forcing theorem to obtain a new-real name and a condition before applying the perfect-tree lemma. To transfer universal measurability to R^3, explicitly build the three-stream Borel bijection on the conull canonical-code domain, prove Borel and null preservation from cylinder measures and product completion, and transfer the Borel-mod-null witness in both directions. Then repeat the displayed ZF+DC consequence arguments with L(R) in place of M; no HOD(S)-specific theorem is applied across models.

references.title: Solovay, A model of set-theory in which every set of reals is Lebesgue measurable
references.locator: Theorem 1 and Parts II-III, printed pp.1-2 and 29-53; the homogeneous proof applied to L(R)

references.title: Unger, A Brief Account of Solovay's Model
references.locator: L(R) alternative and regularity adaptation, pp.1-2

items.axiom_audit: The target conclusions are internal to ZF+DC; the inaccessible and ambient AC remain construction hypotheses.

items.title: Fixed finite-fragment verification for the Solovay construction
items.statement: For every externally fixed finite fragment Delta of the stated ZF+DC universal-regularity theory, including failure of Choice and the named exclusions, ZFC plus an inaccessible proves that a set model of Delta exists. No PA-verified uniform proof-code transformer is asserted.
items.strategy: Trace the fixed finite target formulas through the Solovay proofs, reflect the resulting finite source family above an inaccessible, collapse a countable elementary hull containing that inaccessible, build a generic for the countable forcing model, and execute the retained construction. Keep the quantifier over Delta external.
items.axiom_base: External fixed-fragment transfer from ZFC plus an inaccessible

items.title: Solovay-model regularity is consistent relative to an inaccessible cardinal
items.statement: Con(ZFC+an inaccessible) implies Con(ZF+DC+universal LM+BP+PSP+not AC), including the stated absence of Vitali/Bernstein sets, Hamel bases, discontinuous additive maps, and Banach–Tarski decompositions. No converse or internal inaccessible is asserted.
items.strategy: Apply the externally indexed finite-fragment model-transfer theorem to the repaired Solovay construction. For each fixed finite target fragment, use its reflected countable transitive source model and conversion into a set model of that fragment. Keep the inaccessible solely in the antecedent and make no uniform arithmetic proof-transformer claim.

title: Solovay's Model and Regularity of All Sets of Reals: Examples and Counterexamples

items.title: Factoring the Solovay collapse around a real parameter
items.statement: Given t in V[G_xi], display the initial/tail factorization and the absorbed factorization V[G]=V[t][H].
items.strategy: Track complete suborders, quotient forcing, the collapse map coding G_xi, and which parameters tail homogeneity may decide.

items.title: A Borel representative from a random Boolean value
items.statement: For phi(x,a), trace the random-algebra Boolean value at the generic-real name to its Borel representative.
items.strategy: Form the Boolean value of the assertion that the top of the homogeneous tail forces phi. Evaluate that assertion at each N-random x, then use the tail's 0-or-1 Boolean value and its actual generic to obtain final-extension truth. Mark the nongeneric exception before quotienting modulo null; do not assert N[x]-to-V[G] absoluteness for arbitrary phi.

items.title: Perfect-tree splitting of a new-real name
items.statement: Work through three levels of the perfect tree making new-real-name interpretations pairwise distinct.
items.strategy: Derive the splitting-below-every-condition claim from forcing decision density and the newness hypothesis. At stage n meet every dense requirement of index at most n at each node and every ordered pair, preserving earlier requirements by downward closure, and decide prefixes of length at least n; display the continuity modulus.

items.title: Coding countably many Solovay definition parameters
items.statement: Interleave countably many countable ordinal parameters into the one sequence used for HOD(S) closure.
items.strategy: Use a fixed pairing of omega squared with omega, alternate formula/ordinal codes, and decode uniformly. This directly instantiates the HOD(S) parameter convention and does not invoke the separate omega-closure theorem.
items.axiom_base: ZF after ambient witnesses are chosen

items.title: How universal regularity excludes the classical Choice pathologies
items.statement: Compare the distinct contradictions for Vitali selectors, Bernstein sets, Hamel bases, and discontinuous additive functions.
items.strategy: Tabulate: translation/measurability, PSP, nonmeasurable coefficient kernel, and measurable-Cauchy regularity; record DC's measure role.

items.title: The volume contradiction for an alleged Banach–Tarski decomposition
items.statement: Write the full finite-additivity calculation V=2V for an alleged equidecomposition.
items.strategy: Derive internal Countable Choice from DC, then name pieces and motions, sum original and target volumes, apply invariance termwise, and insert 0<V<infinity.

items.title: Solovay's model proves that an inaccessible cardinal exists
items.statement: The construction's inaccessible is an external source-theory hypothesis, and the ambient collapse makes kappa equal to omega_1. The relative-consistency theorem does not say that the target theory, or M internally, proves any inaccessible exists.
items.strategy: Use the ambient collapse computation and the same-reals/ordinals theorems to prove that the designated kappa is omega_1 in both inner models, then inspect the one-way formal Con implication. Make no assertion that either target model has no other inaccessible ordinal.
